instruction:
Copy `/home/user/Desktop/porous_base/` to `/home/user/Desktop/porous/` and solve a fixed packed-bed pressure-drop case with OpenFOAM from the command line. Source the installed OpenFOAM environment before running OpenFOAM commands. On this machine, before running the case, load OpenFOAM with `source /opt/openfoam11/etc/bashrc`; the solver binaries are under `/opt/openfoam11/bin` and its platform bin directory.

Build a `1 x 0.1 x 0.01 m` rectangular domain with exactly `(100 10 1)` cells, symmetry at the y boundaries and empty front/back faces. Use water with reference density `1000 kg/m^3`, kinematic viscosity `1e-6 m^2/s`, a uniform inlet velocity `(0.1 0 0)` m/s, and zero kinematic pressure at the outlet. Select all 1,000 cells into the cell zone `porosity` using `topoSet`. Apply an isotropic Darcy-Forchheimer model to that entire zone with `d=(1e8 1e8 1e8) 1/m^2`, `f=(1000 1000 1000) 1/m`, and coordinate axes aligned with the global axes. Run `blockMesh`, require a successful `checkMesh`, run `topoSet`, and solve laminar flow for exactly 500 SIMPLE iterations using `porousSimpleFoam`, retaining ASCII iteration-500 `U` and `p`. Save outputs as `/home/user/Desktop/porous/log.blockMesh`, `log.checkMesh`, `log.topoSet`, and `log.porousSimpleFoam`; a failed mesh check is not acceptable. Write final cell centres `C` and save that output as `log.writeCellCentres`. At every distinct cell-centre x-coordinate, average kinematic pressure over the 10 cross-sectional cells. Define `delta_p` in Pa as `1000 * (p_mean at the first x station - p_mean at the last x station)`. Create `/home/user/Desktop/postprocess.py` that reads the final `C` and `p`, writes all 100 axial stations to `/home/user/Desktop/axial_pressure.csv` with columns `x_m,p_kinematic_m2ps2,p_pa`, and writes `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as one line containing `delta_p`. Do not hard-code the result and do not use GUI tools.
